Hi Karthik / Priya —

Thanks for the kickoff earlier. Attached is our working MAP (QuantMed_MAP_v3.xlsx) with expected timelines and evaluation criteria. High-level asks from our side:
- Production target: 250 inference requests/sec (99th percentile traffic profile) with p95 latency < 200ms for single-turn queries.
- Geo: primary traffic from us-west (telemetry heavy), failover to us-east. EU presence required for a later phase.
- Preference: Dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs; private deployment for PHI-scoped workflows.

Can you confirm preliminary sizing (GPU type/count) and an initial throughput runbook for the evaluation plan? We want weekly MAP checkpoints every Tuesday to keep the timeline (goal: go-live by 2026-06-30).

Also attaching a SOC2 evidence request (see separate PDF) procurement will kick off once we have the sizing + pricing.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — capacity targets and next steps

Alex — thanks, we reviewed the MAP and did a quick pass on sizing. Initial read (high level):

Proposed baseline configuration (can iterate after bench/soak tests):
- US-West (primary, low-latency): 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB (serving peak requests) + 8 x NVIDIA A100 40GB (steady-state burst/fallback).
- US-East (failover / warm standby): 6 x NVIDIA A100 40GB.
- EU (Dublin) - optional private pool for PHI: 4 x NVIDIA A100 40GB (customer-managed private deployment).

Throughput targets per pool (initial):
- US-West H100 pool: target 180-220 req/s (with aggressive batching + KV cache).
- US-West A100 pool: target 60-90 req/s as fallback (lower throughput but cost efficient).
- Combined steady-state target: ~250 req/s with autoscaling and cross-region spill.

Key assumptions and knobs we plan to validate in evaluation plan:
- Model: 70B param open model (quantized) — token length distribution from your MAP.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with 15-50ms batch delay windows; payload-level prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- KV cache sizing: reserve 128GB per H100 instance for large chat histories.

Initial action items (owners):
- laura_bennett: run baseline latency/throughput bench (per-region) and deliver initial numbers by 2026-04-05.
- marissa_cole: produce cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private options and include egress & peering by 2026-04-09.
- vivek_kulkarni: validate VPC peering approach and any network egress constraints (impact on latency) by 2026-04-08.
- karthik_iyer: produce runbook for soak test and success criteria by 2026-04-06.

Let's sync Tuesday for the weekly checkpoint; I'll circulate a short agenda focusing on throughput validation, costs, and timeline risks.

Thanks,

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — baseline benchmarks and updated targets

Team / Alex — did the quick bench runs against a 70B quantized model (replicating token mix from MAP). Highlights:

- Single H100 80GB (optimized kernels, dynamic batching): median latency 95ms, p95 190ms, p99 260ms at 16 concurrent streams (batch size avg 18). Sustained tokens/sec ~1,800 (varies by prompt length).
- Single A100 40GB: median 160ms, p95 320ms, p99 450ms at similar concurrency; tokens/sec ~1,100.

Implications:
- To meet p95<200ms for the overall service we need H100s in the hot pool for latency-sensitive traffic; A100s can serve bulk/batch workloads and lower-cost background inference.
- Combined pool sizing (recommended for initial eval): US-West: H100 x6 + A100 x6 gives headroom for 250 req/s with buffer and autoscale triggers.

Updated action items / short-term tests:
- 2-hr soak test (combined pool) scheduled: 2026-04-09 02:00-04:00 UTC — owner: laura_bennett (deliverable: soak report).
- Verify prefix/KV cache hit rates on representative chat sessions — owner: vivek_kulkarni (due 2026-04-08).
- Cost delta summary for H100-first topology vs A100-primary — owner: marissa_cole (deliverable: preliminary cost delta by 2026-04-09).

I'll upload the bench logs and sample dashboards to the MAP folder after the soak.

Laura Bennett
Performance Engineering — Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya / Procurement / Team — quick recap from our weekly MAP checkpoint and next steps (consolidated):

Decisions (agreed):
- Primary topology: US-West (us-west-2) H100-first pool. Final recommended initial sizing: 6 x NVIDIA H100 80GB (hot) + 6 x NVIDIA A100 40GB (warm/cost-efficient).
- Failover: US-East A100 pool (6 x A100) for regional spill and DR.
- EU requirement: Private Dedicated pool in Dublin (customer-managed) with 4 x A100 40GB for PHI workflows (timing: phase 2).
- Throughput targets: combined steady-state ~250 req/s; p95 latency target <= 200ms with H100 hot pool.

Timeline:
- Procurement + SOC2 due diligence: target sign-off by 2026-04-15.
- Staging environment (bench + soak tests): by 2026-05-15.
- Go-live (production): target 2026-06-30.

Open risks / notes:
- p99 remains sensitive; we'll use autoscaling + spill to reduce tail latency. p99 mitigation plan owned by laura_bennett.
- Network egress for private pool needs validation for PHI pathing — vivek_kulkarni to confirm.

Action items (owner — due):
- laura_bennett — deliver soak test report (2-hr soak) and p99 mitigation plan — due 2026-04-10.
- marissa_cole — pricing delta (H100-first vs A100-primary) including egress & peering costs — due 2026-04-09.
- vivek_kulkarni — VPC peering design and PHI egress constraints; provide diagram & E2E latency estimates — due 2026-04-08.
- karthik_iyer — finalize runbook and coordinate procurement docs (DocuSign + HubSpot link) — due 2026-04-12.

Thanks everyone — see you at next week's checkpoint.
